page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-64xCPU-384GB is a Cloud Native family virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 64 vCPUs mapped to 64 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7542 processor with an x86_64 architecture. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz with a shared allocation model. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, providing 6.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include any local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate a clear contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is limited, with stress-ng single-core CPU tests scoring in the bottom 10% and single-threaded gzip and bzip3 compression/decompression falling in the bottom 25%. However, multi-threaded operations leverage the high core count effectively; bzip3 multi-threaded decompression, Passmark CPU scores, and Passmark CPU extended instructions, encryption, and physics tests all rank in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth for cached small blocks also scores in the top 25%, while large-block read and write bandwidth remain in the middle 50%.

The shared CPU allocation model offers a cost-efficient path to high memory capacity and high core density, making it suitable for parallelizable workloads that do not require sustained, dedicated single-core performance. Tradeoffs include the lack of local storage and poor single-core execution speeds. This server is appropriate for multi-threaded data processing, memory-intensive applications, static web serving, and moderate database operations.
